findings.text: The restructured `except (OSError, ValueError)` now encloses the checkout context managers entered at lines 1213-1229. `BaseCheckoutError` subclasses `ValueError` (landing_measure.py:1592), so a base checkout that cannot be built is caught here and reported as "the measurement raised BaseCheckoutError: could not create a scratch tree for ..." instead of by the outer handler at line 1288 as "the base checkout could not be built: ...". Verified: tests/test_the_landing_pass_measures_and_lands.py::test_an_unusable_scratch_root_refuses_that_run_and_returns passes at dd1ff29 and fails at 366cfd21. The head reddens an existing test and a checkout failure is now attributed to the measurement, which is exactly the misattribution its sibling test (test_a_measurement_error_is_not_reported_as_a_checkout_failure) exists to prevent in the other direction.

The added `trap 'exit 143' TERM INT` (here and at line 222) is the only path that removes a submitted job's tree when the scheduler ends the job by signal, and no test sends TERM or INT to the job script; the killed-process case in the new test covers the next-pass scratch sweep instead. A regression that dropped the trap would redden no assertion, so the commit's signal claim is unguarded.

notes: Independent reproduction of the blocking finding: the reviewed head was extracted with `git archive 366cfd21665ccc1c64e8fb8ca3aee83efb23eea5` to a scratch tree and the base with dd1ff2909ce0bc420a93eac425c435f48b02cf76; `PYTHONPATH=<tree> <repo>/.venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider` ran both files that import the changed modules. Head: 1 failed, 26 passed. Base: the failing case passed. Logs kept in this run's scratch directory. The reviewed run's baseline_suite and after_suite arms both record 0 failures over two overlapping sets of three files, so added_failure_count is 0 from those logs; the failing importer test was not in either arm and the done_when required it.
